question: By which Constitutional Amendment Act can the same person be appointed as the Governor of two or more states?
solution:
The correct answer is the __**7th Constitutional Amendment Act**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The 7th Constitutional Amendment Act of 1956 allows the same person to be appointed as the Governor of two or more states in India.
 
• This amendment is related to the reorganization of states. 
 
• When a person is appointed as the Governor of more than one state, the President determines how the emoluments and allowances are shared between the states.
 
• The person is also entitled to any other emoluments, allowances, and privileges that Parliament may determine

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• 9th Constitutional Amendment Act
 
• This act of 1960 gave the President the power to suspend the operation of any article or provision of the National Capital Territory. 
 
• 11th Constitutional Amendment Act
 
• This act of 1961 changed the process for electing the Vice-President.
 
• The Vice-President is now elected by members of both Houses of Parliament in a joint meeting. 
 
• 18th Constitutional Amendment Act
 
• This act was passed in 1966.
